name: NY-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Goldman lost renomination, with Lander's strong fundraising
Republican nominee has minimal reported fundraising
model.rationale: The seat's +32 Democratic lean and a 98% Democratic price on Polymarket make a Republican upset implausible even with the incumbent off the ballot. Lander's $2.5 million in fundraising against a Republican with no reported money reinforces the Safe D call.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican outside spending or an unexpected third-party dynamic could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Brooklyn-based House seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly +32. Dan Goldman lost his renomination, and Democrat Brad Lander enters the general as the heavy favorite after raising about $2.5 million. Republican Jennifer Moore has no reported fundraising or cash on hand.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 98 percent, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the high twenties.
